agents.goal: Inspect the raw e-commerce churn dataset and produce an exact quality report: missing values per column, category spellings, outliers and the churn rate. Every number in the report must come from the profiling tool's output.

tasks.description:
Profile the raw dataset at {raw_data_path} (sheet "E Comm") with the profile_raw_data tool. The tool writes {output_dir}/quality_report.json.
From the tool output, summarise for the team: - row count, duplicate rows and whether CustomerID is unique - duplicates once CustomerID is ignored: quote the tool's
  duplicates_ignoring_id.summary sentence word for word, then give the
  churn rate in duplicate groups. Do not combine the counts in your own
  words. Say plainly that "duplicate rows: 0" only holds because every
  row has its own id
- every column with missing values: count, share, and churn rate when the
  value is missing versus present
- every categorical column with each spelling, its count and churn rate,
  pointing out spellings that look like the same meaning; they are kept
  as separate categories because their churn rates differ, so report the
  difference without guessing its cause (do not call it a data-entry error)
- numeric outliers the tool flagged - the overall churn rate
Use only numbers that appear in the tool output. Do not recommend imputing, merging categories or clipping outliers: the team decided against all three.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown quality summary with sections Overview, Missing values, Categories, Outliers and Target, where every number matches quality_report.json.

agents.goal: Produce clean_data.csv as a faithful copy of the raw data: keep every missing value as missing, keep every category spelling as it is, keep outliers, and prove with the comparison tool that no value changed. Document every decision in the preparation log.

tasks.description:
Create the handoff file with the export_clean_data tool: it reads sheet "E Comm" from {raw_data_path}, writes {output_dir}/clean_data.csv without changing any value, re-reads the CSV and compares it to the raw data cell by cell, and returns the comparison result and the file's sha256.
The team decisions you must follow and document: - missing values stay missing (no imputation, no synthetic values) - category spellings stay as they are (no merging) - outliers stay as they are (no clipping or removal)
If the tool reports any difference between the CSV and the raw data, say so plainly at the top of the log and do not describe the file as faithful.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown preparation log with sections Source, Steps, Decisions, Verification (the tool's comparison result and the sha256) and Output.

agents.goal: Produce an exploratory analysis report with charts and descriptive statistics, and write business insights that tell the retention team which customer groups churn most and what that means for the discount budget.

tasks.description:
Run the run_eda tool on {output_dir}/clean_data.csv. It writes {output_dir}/eda_report.html with descriptive statistics, distributions and churn-rate charts, and returns the computed churn rates by group.
Then write business insights for Harbor & Vale's retention team: - which customer groups churn most, with their size and churn rate - what that means for where the discount budget should go - spellings that look like the same meaning (for example COD and Cash on
  Delivery): they are kept as separate categories because their churn
  rates differ; report both rates and do not guess the cause (do not call
  it a data-entry error or say the groups behave the same)
- missing values whose churn rate differs from present values - rows repeated under a new CustomerID: quote the tool's
  duplicates_ignoring_id sentence word for word (do not combine the counts
  in your own words), and say that every copy is counted as a separate
  customer in the group sizes and churn rates above
- SatisfactionScore and the other score columns have no documented
  direction (the data dictionary does not say whether 5 is best or
  worst), so name the score value (for example "score 5"), never "lowest"
  or "highest" satisfaction
- the known limitation that the churn window is undefined, so last-month
  columns may describe customers after they churned

Quote only numbers the tool returned. Do not claim causation.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown insights document with an executive summary of three to five bullet points, then sections Who churns, Budget implications, Data caveats.

agents.goal: Publish dataset_contract.json, the only interface the Data Scientist crew may rely on. The numbers (types, ranges, means, null counts, allowed values, row count, sha256) come from the contract tool; you add only the text fields: column descriptions, assumptions and leakage notes.

tasks.description:
Use the build_contract tool on {output_dir}/clean_data.csv. It computes every number of the contract (types, ranges, means, null counts, allowed values, row count, target rate, sha256) and returns the column list.
Your part is the text the tool cannot know. Return: - a one-sentence description for every column, based on the data
  dictionary sheet "Data Dict" in {raw_data_path} and the tool output
- the assumptions the Data Scientist crew must know: no imputation, no
  category merging, outliers kept, duplicate rows kept (rows repeated
  under a new CustomerID, exactly or with one value changed; counts are in
  the tool output under dataset), and which units are assumed
  (Tenure in months, WarehouseToHome in km, CashbackAmount in INR)
- leakage notes: the churn window is undefined, so Complain, CouponUsed,
  OrderCount, CashbackAmount and PreferedOrderCat (all "last month") may
  leak; the different spellings with different churn rates; and the
  duplicate rows, which leak between train and test unless each group of
  copies stays on one side of the split

Do not return or change any number; the code merges your text with the tool's numbers into {output_dir}/dataset_contract.json.
tasks.expected_output: Column descriptions for all 20 columns, a list of assumptions and a list of leakage notes, in the structured format requested.

agents.goal: Confirm that clean_data.csv matches dataset_contract.json before any modeling starts, and tell the team exactly which columns may be used, which are forbidden, and which assumptions and leakage risks come with them.

tasks.description:
Use the review_contract tool on {input_dir}. It validates clean_data.csv against dataset_contract.json and returns whether it passes, every violation, the target, the usable features, the forbidden features, the duplicate-row counts, the assumptions and the leakage notes.
If the tool reports any violation, put "CONTRACT FAILED" on the first line, list every violation with its message, and say that modeling must not start. Otherwise report: - the contract version, row count and target with its expected rate - the usable features with type and unit, marking units that are assumed - the forbidden features and why they are excluded - the duplicate rows: quote the tool's duplicates_summary sentence word
  for word (do not combine the counts in your own words), then say what
  they mean for the train/test split
- the assumptions and leakage notes the model card must carry
Use only numbers that appear in the tool output.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown contract review with sections Verdict, Target, Features, Excluded columns, Duplicates, Assumptions and leakage.

agents.goal: Build features.csv from the contract alone: numeric features unchanged with their missing values, one 0/1 column per allowed category value, no forbidden columns, and explain every choice in the feature log.

tasks.description:
Use the build_features tool with input_dir {input_dir} and output_dir {output_dir}. It writes {output_dir}/features.csv from clean_data.csv using only the contract, and refuses to run if the data does not match it.
Document in the feature log: - how each source column became features (unchanged or one-hot) and the
  number of feature columns
- that missing values are kept (give the count) because both models handle
  them natively, and that no value was imputed
- that every category spelling has its own column, so spellings with
  different churn rates stay separate
- that CustomerID is excluded from the features, and that duplicate_group
  is a split key, not a feature: it labels rows that are copies of each
  other under different CustomerIDs
- the leakage risk of the last-month columns, which stay in by team decision
Use only numbers that appear in the tool output.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown feature log with sections Inputs, Features, Missing values, Categories, Excluded columns and Leakage risk.

agents.goal: Train HistGradientBoosting and RandomForest, choose one by cross-validated PR-AUC on the training split, and report its test PR-AUC and Recall against the team's quality thresholds, with every number taken from the tool.

tasks.description:
Use the train_and_evaluate tool on {output_dir}. It trains HistGradientBoosting and RandomForest on features.csv, keeps each group of duplicate rows on one side of the 80/20 split, selects one model by cross-validated PR-AUC on the training split, evaluates it once on the test split and saves {output_dir}/model.joblib.
Write the evaluation report: - the split: method, train and test rows, churn rate in each, and the
  number of duplicate groups on both sides (it must be 0)
- both candidates: cross-validated PR-AUC (mean and std) and test PR-AUC,
  Recall, Precision and ROC-AUC, in one table
- which model was selected and by which rule - the selected model's confusion matrix at the decision threshold, in
  words a retention manager understands (churners caught, churners
  missed, loyal customers flagged by mistake)
- test PR-AUC and Recall against the quality thresholds, and whether the
  model meets them; compare PR-AUC with the baseline (the test churn rate)
- the top features by permutation importance, described as what the model
  relies on, not as causes of churn

Quote only numbers the tool returned.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown evaluation report with sections Split, Candidates, Selected model, Quality thresholds and Feature importance.

agents.goal: Write the model card the retention team and reviewers read before they use the model: intended use, data, features, metrics, thresholds, assumptions, leakage risks and limitations.

tasks.description:
Use the read_model_facts tool with input_dir {input_dir} and output_dir {output_dir}. It returns the contract's dataset, target, assumed units, assumptions and leakage notes, the feature summary and the evaluation metrics.
Write a model card for Harbor & Vale's retention team with: - model details: selected model, decision threshold, model file - intended use: ranking customers by churn risk to target retention
  discounts; out of scope: decisions about a single customer without
  human review
- training data: source file, sha256, rows, churn rate, contract version,
  and the duplicate rows (quote the tool's duplicates_summary sentence word
  for word) and how the split handles them
- features: count, encoding, missing values kept, forbidden columns - metrics: test PR-AUC, Recall, Precision and ROC-AUC, the baseline, and
  the quality thresholds with pass or fail
- assumptions, including the assumed units - risks and limitations: the undefined churn window and last-month
  columns, category spellings with different churn rates, duplicates,
  and that the contract must pass before the model is used on new data

Quote only numbers the tool returned. Do not claim causation.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown model card with sections Model details, Intended use, Training data, Features, Metrics, Assumptions, Risks and limitations.

agents.goal: Give a Harbor & Vale retention agent a one-page briefing on one customer before they make contact: how likely the customer is to churn, what the company's own playbook and discount policy say to do for this kind of customer, what not to do, and what is happening in its market this week.

tasks.description:
Prepare a retention briefing for customer {customer_id}.
1. Call customer_risk_profile with customer_id {customer_id}. 2. For every entry in the profile's situations, call search_internal_docs
   once with that entry's query, exactly as given. Do not search for
   anything else.
3. Call search_recent_news once with the profile's news_query, exactly as
   given, for market news from the last 48 hours.
4. Write the briefing from what the documents say about those situations.
   Where two rules apply, follow the order the documents give (for
   example, a complaint is resolved before any offer is made, and a new
   customer gets no discount on the first contact). Apply a rule only to
   the situations the profile lists: a search can return sections about
   other situations (for example a new-customer rule for a low-risk
   customer), and those do not apply.

Rules: - Quote the risk score exactly as the tool returned it, with its band. - If scored_out_of_sample is false, say the score comes from a customer the
  model was trained on.
- List the key facts with their values only. Do not label a value as low,
  high, good, bad or urban: the scales are not documented.
- Every recommendation ends with its source, copied from the search
  result's cite_as field, for example [discount_policy.md > Approval levels].
  Cite only sections the search returned.
- Offers must stay within the discount policy; say who must approve them.
  If the documents say no offer applies, say there is no offer.
- In Market now, list up to three articles the news search returned, each
  as [title](url) with its source and date, and one sentence on what it
  may mean for this customer's retention (for example a competitor's sale
  in their category). If the search returned no articles or an error, write
  "No market news from the last 48 hours was available." Never invent a
  headline or a link.
- Never suggest telling the customer their churn score. - Use only facts from the two tools. Do not claim causes of churn. - At most 420 words: short bullets, no closing paragraph. Recommended
  action has at most five bullets; Market now lists at most three
  articles, one line each.
tasks.expected_output: A markdown briefing of at most 420 words with the sections Customer snapshot, Churn risk, Recommended action, Offer, Do not, Market now (last 48 hours), and Sources (each cite_as value used).
